# Cookbook

The Cookbook is where you go once you know what ArmorIQ does and want to see a complete, working agent built with it, start to finish, including the platform setup around the code.

Each recipe is self-contained: you can clone it, run it, and adapt it, without reading the rest of the SDK docs first.

## How recipes are organized

Every recipe lives at `recipes/<what runs the agent>/<language>/<scenario>/` and describes itself in a `recipe.yaml` (see `schema/recipe.schema.json` for the fields and `schema/taxonomy.yaml` for the allowed values). The tables above are generated from those files.

To check your changes before opening a PR (Node 20 or later):

```bash
npm ci
npm run index           # regenerate the tables above
npm run check           # schema fixtures, every recipe.yaml, and a fresh index
npm run check:recipes   # build each recipe and run its offline test (no API keys needed)
```

Every recipe can run offline with no accounts: `cd` into it and run `npm install && npm run demo:offline`. CI runs the same checks on every PR, building only the recipes the PR touches.
